```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4)
```

A common question in faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) studies is
whether, and for how long, a recipient's microbiome comes to resemble their
donor's. This vignette shows how to measure that with
`akeR(mode = "reference")` and plot it.

It uses `fmt_example`, a **simulated** dataset, so the true answer is known:
two sites, each with 3 donors and 12 recipients sampled before FMT (day 0)
and on days 7, 30 and 90. Responders acquire many donor taxa, which fades
slowly; one recipient per donor is a non-responder. See `?fmt_example` for
details. The last section shows the same analysis on real data from
curatedMetagenomicData.

```{r setup}
library(akeR)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

data(fmt_example)
counts <- fmt_example$counts
md <- fmt_example$metadata
table(md$cohort, md$timepoint)
```

## The `reference` column

Reference mode needs one metadata column, by default called `reference`,
that gives for each sample the ID of the sample to compare it with. IDs must
be sample names in the count table. Samples with `NA` are not compared;
here those are the donors themselves.

```{r}
head(md[, c("subject_id", "role", "timepoint", "reference")], 8)
```

A different column name can be given with `column`.

## Distance to donor over time

```{r}
fmt <- akeR(counts, md, mode = "reference", method = "jaccard")
head(fmt[, c("sample", "reference", "distance", "comparison",
  "timepoint")])
```

Each recipient sample is compared with its own donor (`own`) and with every
other donor (`other`), and all of the sample's metadata is attached. The
other donors are a useful baseline: if recipients become closer to their
own donor than to other donors, the change is specific to that donor, which
is evidence of engraftment rather than a general shift towards a healthy
microbiome.

Each recipient has one `own` distance but several `other` distances, so
take the median of those first, so each sample counts once:

```{r}
per_sample <- aggregate(distance ~ sample + subject_id + timepoint +
  comparison + cohort + responder, data = fmt, FUN = median)

ggplot(per_sample, aes(timepoint, distance, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15),
    size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Jaccard distance to donor", fill = "Donor")
```

Or with ggpubr:

```{r}
ggboxplot(per_sample, x = "timepoint", y = "distance",
  fill = "comparison", palette = "jco", add = "jitter",
  ylab = "Jaccard distance to donor", xlab = "")
```

Before FMT, recipients are about as far from their own donor as from
others. After FMT they move much closer to their own donor.

### Following each recipient

Because the metadata is attached, the distances are easy to split by any
other variable. Following each recipient over time shows the simulated
responders moving towards their donor and the non-responders staying put:

```{r}
own <- fmt[fmt$comparison == "own", ]

ggplot(own, aes(day, distance, group = subject_id, colour = responder)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Jaccard distance to own donor",
    colour = "Responder")
```

## Watch out for cohort effects

The "other" donors include donors from both sites. Samples from the same
site tend to be more alike anyway (same population, protocols and
sequencing), so recipients can look closer to their own donor simply
because that donor is from their own site. Look up each reference's site
to see this:

```{r}
fmt$reference_cohort <- md[fmt$reference, "cohort"]
fmt$donor_type <- ifelse(fmt$comparison == "own", "own donor",
  ifelse(fmt$reference_cohort == fmt$cohort, "other donor, same site",
    "other donor, other site"))

day0 <- fmt[fmt$timepoint == "day_0", ]
ggboxplot(day0, x = "donor_type", y = "distance", fill = "donor_type",
  palette = "jco", add = "jitter", legend = "none", xlab = "",
  ylab = "Jaccard distance at day 0",
  order = c("own donor", "other donor, same site",
    "other donor, other site"))
```

Before FMT, recipients are as far from their own donor as from other
donors at the same site, but further from donors at the other site. So
when comparing own and other donors, use donors from the same site (or
analyse each site separately). Day 0 is a built-in negative control: there
should be no own-donor effect before the transplant.

## The metric matters

Presence/absence metrics such as Jaccard track which donor taxa are
acquired, while abundance-weighted metrics such as Bray-Curtis are
dominated by a few abundant taxa. Plot the own-donor distances with several
metrics:

```{r, fig.width = 8}
metrics <- c("jaccard", "aitchison", "bray", "robust.aitchison")
by_metric <- do.call(rbind, lapply(metrics, function(m) {
  res <- akeR(counts, md, method = m)
  res <- res[res$comparison == "own", ]
  data.frame(method = m, timepoint = res$timepoint,
    responder = res$responder, distance = res$distance)
}))

ggplot(by_metric, aes(timepoint, distance, fill = responder)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Distance to own donor", fill = "Responder")
```

The simulation changes both which taxa are present and their abundances,
so all four metrics show the effect here; in real data they often
disagree. Report the metric you chose and why, and check that the
conclusion holds with at least one alternative.

## A different reference: the recipient's own baseline

Any sample can be a reference. To see how far each recipient has moved from
their pre-FMT state, point a column at the same subject's day 0 sample:

```{r}
baseline <- md[md$day %in% 0, ]
md$baseline <- baseline$sample_id[match(md$subject_id, baseline$subject_id)]
md$baseline[md$baseline == md$sample_id] <- NA  # day 0 itself

from_base <- akeR(counts, md, mode = "reference", column = "baseline",
  method = "jaccard")
from_base <- from_base[from_base$comparison == "own", ]

ggplot(from_base, aes(timepoint, distance, fill = responder)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Jaccard distance from baseline", fill = "Responder")
```

Here the `other` rows, dropped above, would be the distances to other
recipients' baselines.

## A single reference for everyone

If every sample should be compared with the same sample (one donor, a mock
community, or a pooled sample), put that ID in every row:

```{r}
md$single <- ifelse(md$role == "donor", NA, "D01_donor")
single <- akeR(counts, md, column = "single", method = "jaccard")
head(single[, c("sample", "reference", "distance", "timepoint")])
```

## Do recipients of the same donor look alike?

Group mode answers this, grouping by donor. Use day 30 only (one sample per
recipient), and keep only pairs of recipients from the same site, since
donors are nested in sites:

```{r}
day30 <- md[md$timepoint %in% "day_30", ]
same_donor <- akeR(counts[, rownames(day30)], day30, mode = "group",
  column = "donor_id", method = "jaccard")
same_donor <- same_donor[same_donor$cohort_1 == same_donor$cohort_2, ]

ggboxplot(same_donor, x = "comparison", y = "distance",
  fill = "comparison", palette = "jco", add = "jitter", legend = "none",
  xlab = "Recipient pairs: same donor vs different donors",
  ylab = "Jaccard distance")
```

## Real data from curatedMetagenomicData

The same analysis on a real FMT study, IaniroG_2022 (Ianiro et al. 2022,
*Nature Medicine*), downloaded from curatedMetagenomicData. Donor samples
list the FMT procedures (`fmt_id`) they supplied, separated by `;`, and
recipients record the procedure they received, so the `reference` column
is built by matching the two. This needs an internet connection, so it is
not run here:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(curatedMetagenomicData)

tse <- curatedMetagenomicData("IaniroG_2022.relative_abundance",
  counts = TRUE, dryrun = FALSE)[[1]]
tse <- tse[, !is.na(tse$FMT_role)]

# For each recipient, find the donor sample that supplied their procedure
is_donor <- tse$FMT_role == "donor"
donor_fmt <- strsplit(tse$fmt_id[is_donor], ";", fixed = TRUE)
lookup <- data.frame(
  fmt_id = unlist(donor_fmt),
  donor = rep(colnames(tse)[is_donor], lengths(donor_fmt))
)
tse$reference <- ifelse(is_donor, NA,
  lookup$donor[match(tse$fmt_id, lookup$fmt_id)])

# Keep one clinical cohort, with its recipients and their donors
rec <- tse$subcohort == "IaniroG_2022_CDiff" & !is.na(tse$reference)
tse <- tse[, rec | colnames(tse) %in% tse$reference[rec]]

fmt <- akeR(tse, mode = "reference", method = "jaccard")
ggboxplot(fmt, x = "days_from_first_collection", y = "distance",
  fill = "comparison")
```
